chunks: Their abodes turned into graves, and their wealth into inheritable estate. They do not know who came to them, nor do they pay heed to those who weep over them, nor do they respond to those who call them. Therefore, beware of this world, for it is treacherous, deceitful, and cheating; it gives and takes back, covers with clothes and uncovers. Its pleasure does not last, its hardship does not end, and its calamity does not stop.

key_terms.أَجْدَاثاً: plural of grave, meaning tombs or burial places

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the worldly life (dunya) according to this narration?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) uses the vivid imagery of graves as 'pits' and wealth as mere inheritance to illustrate the total severance of connection with the living, emphasizing the transient nature of dunya. This passage, found in the section on those apprehensive of death, serves as a spiritual warning against the deceptive allure of worldly pleasures, urging believers to recognize its fleeting ease and enduring trials. It reinforces the Shia concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as renunciation of the world, but as detachment from its deceptive grip.
